text:
Leon Draisaitl has 16 goals in 18 games, and the encouraging part for Edmonton isn't the finishing. It's that he's getting to better ice than a year ago: 1.66 individual expected goals per 60 minutes (the quality of his own shots), up from 1.02 last season. He scored twice on Saturday against Vancouver, has goals in three straight games and points in five straight.

The finishing is the part that will cool. He's shooting 23% against 19% last season, with 16 goals on 10.9 expected, and the Oilers have scored 15.9 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Those gaps usually close. Even so, our range projects 51 goals over the full season (42 to 62), well past the 35 he scored in 65 games last season.

The goals get the headlines; the setups are why his line works. With Draisaitl on at five-on-five, Edmonton owns almost 62% of the expected goals, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists last season. When the shooting percentage comes back to earth, that part of his game won't.
headline: Draisaitl's finishing is hot, but his chances are better
